articles.title: Giant Space Spaghetti Feeds a Hungry Black Hole!
articles.summary: NASA's James Webb telescope spotted long gas noodles flowing into a black hole's spinning dinner plate. The gas moves 600 km per second—that's over 200 times faster than a race car!

articles.title: Japan's Baby Rocket Hops 33 Feet—Just Like SpaceX's First Try!
articles.summary: Japan's RV-X rocket prototype jumped 33 feet high and landed softly after 40 seconds. It's a tiny hop toward building reusable rockets that can fly again and again, like SpaceX's Falcon 9.

articles.title: A Star Ate a Planet—and Scientists Found the Proof in Its Belly!
articles.summary: Star TOI-5882 has way too much lithium, a chemical planets are rich in. Scientists think it gobbled up a planet, maybe pushed by a brown dwarf buddy. The sun might do the same to Earth in 5 billion years!
